body: Hummanaya is one of the places that Sri Lankans will not miss when they are touring the surrounding area. But make sure to check before you go: during some months there will be hardly any water spray coming up through the blow-hole. We were lucky and got to see its full splendour.Locals operate several (paid) vehicle parks - you must park there and then walk the rest of the way. It would've been good to have some signs giving information about the walk: because, from the car park, we had to walk around 200m or so, most of which involved stairs and/or rocky terrain. We were not aware of this and one member of our group who had difficulty climbing stairs had to stop and turn back halfway there. The walkway winds through a fishing village and on either side of the path there are stalls selling dried fish products.There is a viewing area secured with metal bars for safety. The terrain is heavily eroded so watch your step.
title: Famous natural wonder

body: This is a very rare natural phenomena and only available in few places all over the world. Here the air is blown through a small hole at the surface due to pressure differences between a closed underground system and the surface. You need to be bit patient and wait till it occurs. In my experience it happens at least once in 10mins. You need to buy a ticket for a small amount and climb up few steps to reach the place. Parking spaces are available roadside. Best to visit in morning and evening to avoid burning sunshine. There’s a beautiful beach on the way up. Be careful we saw some sea urchins there.
title: Rare natural phenomena, worth a visit

body: You have to go on the right side road after 1 km or so from Dickwella towards Tangalle. There is a parking and from thee you have to walk around 100 m. Foreigners have to pay USD 5 as entrance fee. It is a fishing village and fish are sold by almost by every house.Do not go very close to the blow hole as the you ca get the spray. The water from the waves goes into the rock and as diameter becomes small gains more pressure and comes up through the hole in the stone making seawater to go up in the air giving a sound and a spray of water. Height of the water going up in the air depends on the volume and the speed of the waves. Therefore from July onward, the waves are high and the spray is high too.View towards the sea is is nice as it is from a higher elevation.There is a small restaurant there little refreshments could be bought.and
title: Water Going Up Through a Hole in a Rock Located at the Beach.

body: My husband and I visited this attraction in middle of January and did not know that it is seasonal dependant before we paid the entrance fee to go in. When we arrived to the entrance, the staff there was just interested in collecting the entrance fee of Rs 250 per foreign visitor and did not tell us that we will not be able to see the blow hole experience at this time of year. It was when we did not see any big gushes of waves at the actual blowhole that one of the staff who decided to tag along with us explained that from probably October to May is low tide season and therefore would not be able to see the big gush of water from the blow hole. It is only around June to August that visitors will be able to see the big gush from the blow hole. This information would be nice to know before we visited this site and paid the entrance fee. Without seeing the display of the blow hole in action, there is nothing special about this site that warrants any kind of a fee. There are lots of "free" coastlines along Southern Sri Lanka that would be just as nice. The other annoying thing is that the staff that decided to come with us to the blow hole recommended a spot for us to take pictures (which we could have found ourselves) and then expecting a tip for that. body: Second largest natural blow hole in the world. Located 12 km from Tangalle on a rock about 40 ft above sea level. Once you reached the area locals will look after the vehicle for small fee. As you have to wait for the moment, hat is a must.Due to the strong humming sound it is named as " Hummanaya " .One that shouldn't be missed.

body: Hummanaya is known as the 2nd largest blowhole in the world. Those who travel downsouth, the blowhole is located at Kudawella (around Dickwella) which is around 32km from the Matara -Godagama expressway exit. From the main Tangalle road, route to the blowhole is a bit tricky. You can always seek assistance from the locals to locate it. There are many private parking areas around. You need to park and walk up and down for around 600 - 700 meters. While the hike, there are locals & residents who sell fried fishes, dried fishes and pickles. We grabbed some guava pickle which helped us to much during the 10 minutes walk.You come to a point to buy tickets (Rs. 20/- for locals and Rs. 250/- for foreigners) and then again continue the walk.The blowhole is covered with a safety railing. It shoots up a gust upto nearly 70 - 80 feet. Quite an interesting thing to watch.TIP: Bring water as you become thirsty after the walk. Make sure you wear a cap / hat and a bit of sun cream to be shady under the scorching sun - though there's a lot of shade while walking, the area where the blowhole is doesn't have shade and you just need to stand and wait until it shoot up water.
title: Once a lifetime experience

body: Hike to Dikwella Hummanaya Blow Hole, Sri LankaUnique Blowhole is the only known blowhole in Sri Lanka and it is considered to be the second largest natural blowhole in the world. When the caverns are filled to capacity, the ensuing pressure causes the water to escape through a small hole to form a giant fountain. caused when sea water rushes through a submerged cavern and is pushed upwards. The sea water flows underneath the shore, and then comes out of this hole due to pressure. The water fountain created by the geological feature shoots up every couple of minutes, depending on the nature of the sea, with the spray often reaching as high. & it's without a doubt a beautiful freak of nature. Due to the unique positioning of many rocks, water gets accumulated in a tank like rock pool & with the next wave of water, this entire tank of water gets pressurized & gets pushed above through a small opening on top of the tank creating the blow hole.hummanaya is Located in Mawella, a small town in Dickwella (8km from Dikwella) , the blowhole is completely natural where sea spray due to the high water pressure sprays through a blowhole up to sometimes 10 to 50 feet high. This usually happens during the monsoon season and draws in quite a crowd. The local Municipal council manages the spot and the attending employee is very knowledgeable to read the waves and indicate when one is about to occur and weather its going to be a large one or small...a must visit on your way down south. The road leading up to the Blow Hole is in a bad shape since we had to travel through a shanty area. But this was well worth it once we saw the Hummanaya with its loud hissing sound. The only criticism being the initial approach thru some people backyards..its like walking thru a slum..some sort of clearance needs to be done at that stage but once you get up its nice and pristine.
title: Hummanaya" (Sinhala: හුම්මානය = හූ+මානය)

body: I was excited to see the blow hole as it's something one doesn't see often. However, upon getting there we were told parking would cost. We sent away our tuktuk hoping to get another after the visit. The entrance fee was 250Rs per person which is a lot considering you get to watch a rock formation that supposedly shoots water in the air. Save yourself that money and throw a bucketful of water in the air. Have someone taking a photo. That'll be about the experience you get here. We waited for 30 min with no action except a local guy asking for selfies with us. That was fun. Why they charge for an attraction like this (only worth visiting during specific time) is beyond me. Would be an okay place if it was free. Not worth it.

body: Hummnaya is largest in Sri Lanka and second largest blow hole in the world.Located in small fishing village call Kuda wella.As per my knowledge high season for Hummanaya is July & August and the best time tof day to visit 0800 hrs to 11 hrs and 1500 hrs to 1800 hrs unless the temperature is very high.
title: Second largest blowhole in the world

body: The Blow Hole in Hummanaya is between Tangalle and Dickwella in the southern coastal area of Sri Lanka. You can reach there by either vehicle or trishaw as there is no public bus servince and it is about 2 km out of the main road. Once you reach there you need to pay Rs. 50/- and park your vehicle in the garden of one of the houses as there is no other place to park. There are many vendors selling fried fish, fried prawns and fruits along the road / path. Just bfore the blow hole there is a government office where you need to purchase a ticket. For locals its Rs. 25/- but for foreigners its more. It's advisable to go early morning or towards evening as there is no shade and it gets really warm / hot during the day. The entire journey will take less than an hour. You need to wait patiently for about 1 min to experience the water coming up from the blow hole.
title: A review of the blow hole

body: Stand at the barrier and get wet from the spray, watch the water at it sprays high into the air in gorgeous surroundings. Not too easy to get to but worth the walk up unmade steps to see the wonderful ocean view
title: Exhillarating

body: Hummanaya is the only known blowhole in Sri Lanka and it may be the second largest blowhole in the world. located after Matara and Dikwella town in the Southern Province and at small fishing village called KudawellaYou can see best height in South-west monsoon period. the height of the water blow-up goes up 25 metres (82.0 ft) to 30 metres (98.4 ft).All visitors have to obtain a ticket. 100LKR for foreigners.
title: One and only blow hole in Sri Lanka

body: Thought it was accessible by vehicle ...:) Realised that it was quite a long trek n was very concerned for my mum, dad n uncle who found it hard. You have to park your vehicle and walk. The homeowners in the area allow you to park on their land for a fee of Rs 50/-. The walk is uphill with steps to climb. Then you get to the ticket counter where you purchase a ticket (Rs 20/- for locals and I think it's Rs 250/- for tourists). Thereafter you have to climb uphill (uneven ground) to get to the location. We went in May and I guess it was not the best season for viewing. It blew twice but it was not that spectacular. Felt disspaointed but hey that's nature. I heard that it's most active druing the monsson season. Good to go if you are in the area or passing by.
title: Didnt see much

body: When is the best time to go? Well the blow hole is most active when the seas are at their strongest time. That would be the peak of the south west monsoon period. I asked some residents that we got friendly and we were told that July to August would be the best time to see the blowhole activity and according to my friends who's been here before the water sprouts every minute or so and supposed to be a good sight. When I went in May it was a lull period. 25 rupees is the entrance for locals and 250 for foreigners. I had to wait for 15 mins till it sprouted for the first time and it happened at interests of around 15 mins. The surrounding area is quite beautiful though. The blow hole it self is in high ground and you get a amazing view of the surrounding areas. We took our phantom drones and got some good videos. Now going to hummanaya in the active season brings it drawbacks as well. Firstly Since the seas are rough you wouldn't be able to enjoy the beaches in the south coast. Secondly since it's the off season for tourist in the south west it will be bit more boring to stay in the area. I would only stop by if I was going to Yala or some part of the east coast and I took the southern highway and exited through Matara. Since I am a frequent traveler I think I might get the chance to see it in its peak and will write a review on how it looks during its peak.
title: When is the good time to go!

body: Sat for 25 minutes and nothing happened. Afterwards I asked the guy at ticket desk why they sell tickets if there's nothing to see. He said you have to come at high tide in the right month. He said April is not the right month. So why no information about this and why do they sell you a ticket? Obviously making lots of money as they're just building a massive building and ticket booth. Don't waste your time with this one unless it's 100% the right time/ date/ moon alignment / your feeling lucky etc.
title: Absolute waste of time and money, unless its the right season and conditions.

body: It's a hole in the rock, through which occasionally water is blown into a nice (and refreshing) fountain. When we were there the seas were relatively calm so it wasn't particularly active - so I can understand people's frustration when visiting but it is nature at work and doesn't perform on demand. body: Nice view over the water, the blowhole is just a hole in the rocks where, when the waves hit correctly, water splashes up into the air.

body: I'd read about this blowhole, and as soon as I arrived in the area, tuktuk drivers were offering to take me there, so I decided to go. I had a feeling it wouldn't be that dramatic as the sea was not very rough, but thought it worth a try. When I reached the village nearby, it was disappointingly touristy, with stalls selling all sorts of tat. After a short walk I came to the cliff, where a large cleft is surrounded by new thick silvery railings, which I hadn't expected in a country not known for its Health&Safety laws! I liked the attractive multicoloured rocks, and waited a few moments until the attendant said the waterspout was coming. It just about managed the "hoo" noise, but the water only spurted up about 2 metres, extremely disappointing, though not surprising. The attendant begged me to stay, promising something better, so I waited about 20 minutes, and saw 3 more weak efforts, the highest being about 3 metres. Apparently it can shoot up to 20 metres or more in the right conditions, so it would be worth trying in the height of the monsoon season when the sea would be very rough.. I did actually enjoy the visit, as the views from the cliffs were beautiful.
title: Anticlimax.

body: I'd've liked to have stayed longer but we were on our way to Yala so we had to had to get a move on. It was quite a nice trek to get there, lots of steps & amazing views, & as you can see I got a decent photo of the hole when it blowed.
title: loved this place & ....

body: We visited Hummane Blow Hole recently. It was amazing to witness this unique creation of nature. With a sound like a underground train approaching the sea water is thrown dozens of feet up in the air. The surrounding rock formations were very different to what you normally get to see near the sea. On way to the blow hole you have to climb quite a bit of the way but due to steps this is not hard for the average person. Before the climb starts from the visitor centre there was a lovely patch of beach that was filled with soft sand and isolated. It was a good photo point.
title: Unique

body: Make sure there is a decent swell and its spectacular.Bit of a hike but worth it. I suggest go in morning before busses arrive with hundreds of people and school kids
title: Blows well

body: This is the only blow hole which is available in Sri Lanka & it's without a doubt a beautiful freak of nature. Due to the unique positioning of many rocks, water gets accumulated in a tank like rock pool & with the next wave of water, this entire tank of water gets pressurized & gets pushed above through a small opening on top of the tank creating the blow hole. The road leading up to the Blow Hole is in a bad shape since we had to travel through a shanty area. But this was well worth it once we saw the Hummanaya with its loud hissing sound.
title: A freak of nature

body: Not such a well know attraction and not marketed well at all, but having visited the blow holes in Australia, embarrassingly before seing the one in Sri Lanka...i was amazed at how close to the blow hole one could get..in-fact you can get splashed from the water..so close..and the height of the blow is amazing..the dryer the weather the higher it is. The local Municipal council manages the spot and the attending employee is very knowledgeable to read the waves and indicate when one is about to occur and weather its going to be a large one or small...a must visit on your way down south. The only criticism being the initial approach thru some people backyards..its like walking thru a slum..some sort of clearance needs to be done at that stage but once you get up its nice and pristine.
title: Blow Hole (Hummanaya) : Dikwella.

body: Super Natural wonder in Dikwella and a must see if you are passing by. A bit way in from the main road but worth a visit if you have the time. Amazing to see the water spray naturally depending on how hard the wave is. Much loved by the children as its something new to them. A nice relaxing place to be.
title: Natural Wonder!!!

body: I enjoyed this natural phenomena. When the sea is rough you could experience very high pressured water jest blowing between the two rocks. Be cautious... never go beyond the safety fence.
title: Superb...!!

body: A pleasant spot to stop off and stretch your legs if you are on a long car journey. For the small cost of Rs 200 you gain access to the blow hole. Depending on tides you will get to see and hear the crashing sound of waves hitting the hole in the rocks and shooting up water high in the air. We were lucky to see this sight and got wet each time the water shot up high. There is a small shop where you park the car (small fee) so you can get refreshments and there is a bathroom behind the small information centre.
title: Blow Hole in Kudawella

body: We have visited the Blow Hole twice and in each case it was worth waiting to see it blow, if you watch the rocks below you will be able to anticipate the next time it blows as they disappear under water. Needless to say winds and a high tide make for a wonderful show. They have made quite a few improvements to the area making the site safer but still need to put wire netting round it as the gaps between the rails are a little worrying.If taking small children make sure you keep a tight hold of them. The entry fee is not expensive and remember your entrance fee is going towards better facilities for us tourists in the future. The Environment Centre is interesting and certainly worth a visit but the main attraction is nature's own Blow Hole and no one has any control over when and how high she blows. We were lucky!
title: Worth the wait for it to Blow!

body: many local & foreign attraction. It is worth to view. It could arrange boat trip where can see from sea side while enjoying boat trip.
title: rare view

body: Obviously completely dependant on the tide and the swell at sea. It requires two big waves from different directions to smack into each other at exactly the right place just at the mouth of the channel for a good "BOOM" and a jet of water, spur, steam, to shoot up to 30 m into the air.If its low tide and calm, forget it. If its June monsoon storms, get down there. We were lucky, we saw big stuff in Jan.Lots of crumbly steps, look out.
title: Charming and interesting
Don't waste your time unless it's windy
body: We had to pay to park our van in someones garden and walk through a lane full of stalls selling dried fish. Eventually, past a dead puppy and a few beggars you come to a cash desk in a sort of museum. Up some cobbled steps to a cleft in the cliff. As it was a calm day and the sea was flat so there was nothing blowing through the hole, so we stood there for ten minutes and started walking back. I can imagine when the sea is rough huge spouts of water soaking everyone around and the Sri Lankans thinking that great fun. On the way back to Galle we stopped to photograph a couple of pole fishermen, who immediately jumped off their poles and demanded a tip. I don't think they really ever fished for anything else but tourist tips. We gave the little boy who was with them a really nice set of school stuff, but when no money was forthcoming the older fisherman called me a Saudi, which I found out later meant something not very nice. Charming. Never mind I still love the place,Pedroofpobla

title: blow hall a nice experience
body: The natural blow hall is in awesome stage during the monsoon rain season.The place is located on 183 km post from Colombo on A2 main highway.it is advisable to visit this place before 5.00 pm and avoid going passing the steel fence for safety reason.it will take only 4 hrs from Colombo via express way one way.

title: An impressive place
body: Very impressive place when you have the luck to see the "big wave". You can hear a "hoooo" sound and you can see water like a geyser !I advise you to go there when there is wind, you will have more luck to see the wave.The price is very low, and you can see the wave every nearly 10 minutes (or maybe it was a good day for us...)I recommand this place and you have a beautiful view.Be careful for people who has leg problems, because you have to climb, it's not a big cliff but you have some stairs.Think to take good shoes or not to wear shoes on the rocks.

title: Nice way to support local tourist industry if you are in the area
body: The blow hole was blowing the day we saw it and the kids thought it was grand. We were staying in the Dikwella area, so it wasn't much of a drive to go see it. Overall, I think it is important to support local tourist venues when possible, and this sort of thing, being a natural phenomena is nice enough to see if you have the chance. So, while it's not the thrill of a lifetime, it is an interesting thing to see if you have an afternoon and are in the area.

title: was not lucky
body: the day was not very windy so we did not see anything unfortunatelly. the blow hole did not show any blow :) the fee is 200 rupies per person

title: Truly Exhilarating!
body: The “Hummanya” blow hole is a well-known attraction in the Dikewella region of Sri Lanka. We have to turn right at Kudawella and keep going for about 1 km. Next, we have to climb quite a few shallow steps to reach the point from where this blowhole is visible. On the way up there is a tiny museum and some wash rooms. The view from this point is breathtaking. You can see beautiful rocky cliffs and blue green expanse of water. The blowhole itself is a natural wonder created in the middle of this cliff. There is a gap through which seawater comes gushing up with a loud hoooooooo sound. At that precise moment it gives the impression of a tall fountain. The water pressure builds up more or less every 15 minutes and sometimes the stunning spray can rise as high as 100 feet. Seeing this blow hole is a really heady experience.
